events.title: Head of Design & Innovation, Vice President
events.description: I lead a 5-person Design & Innovation team that owns the strategic features and vision of the SOPHiA DDM™ platform, a deliberate move from large-scale management back to strategic depth. The team works as an R&D unit: we prototype and test ideas before development starts, and we stay accountable for delivery. Our current project is a generative-AI assistant for clinical variant interpretation, designed for regulated healthcare with the clinician confirming every result.
events.descriptionLong:
The team brings together germline and oncology domain experts, platform experts and a UX/UI designer. Some strategic features can't go straight into development, because the problem has to be explored first. So we prototype, test with users, write the requirements, and hand them over to the development teams.

With the team, I conceived and built the variant interpretation assistant and designed the architecture of the harness around the LLM:

  • curated evidence is retrieved at query time;
  • a deterministic grounding gate checks every citation against its source;
  • the model writes a structured draft;
  • nothing is saved until a clinician confirms it.

The domain experts own the prompts, so the clinical reasoning stays with the people who know it. The feature is in development, with an early-access programme planned for December 2026.

I have built much of the platform since its earliest days. That lets me steer these projects across technology, product, design and delivery at once.

I work AI-natively, using Claude for prototyping, coding, requirements and documentation, and I drive internal AI projects beyond the assistant:

  • customer metrics dashboards;
  • Claude skills that help the teams write requirements;
  • a knowledge graph linking the platform documentation and Jira stories, to help people write new stories.

events.title: Head of Platform Product & Engineering
events.description: I led a 25-person organisation (developers, Product Owners, UX/UI designers) owning both product and engineering for the SOPHiA DDM™ platform, and took its new web version to the point where customer migration could start. I set the design direction for clinical users, balancing ease of use with data density, and steered a very large backlog with dashboards that let me arbitrate between new features and moving customers quickly.
events.descriptionLong:
With 5 direct reports, I ran product and engineering as one development organisation, with developers, Product Owners and UX/UI designers working in the same teams. I was also the platform's Product Owner: I aligned stakeholders, defined the user flows and oversaw the frontend architecture.

The design challenge, still open today, is to combine two constraints that pull against each other: making the platform easier to use, and keeping enough information visible at once for clinicians' demanding workflows. A web technology doesn't mean consumer-web conventions, so I chose the web-desktop standard for professional tools, with data density rather than long vertical scrolling.

The backlog mixed new features with parity features from the desktop application. I built dashboards combining Jira, production data and internal sources to decide what came first: staying competitive, or moving users quickly to limit the cost of running two platforms. The same dashboards tracked the development teams' performance.

My engineering background let me make technical calls with the engineers, not only product calls.

Moving a clinical application is not a switch: each customer has validated workflows to carry over. Once the platform was ready, the company put sales, domain experts and product behind the migration, which is on track to close in Q1 2027.

events.title: AI for Medical Diagnosis
events.description: Applied deep learning for medical image analysis, disease detection, and diagnostic model evaluation.

events.title: Head of Platform Product & UX
events.description: I came back to SOPHiA GENETICS to lead a 7-person team of Product Owners and UX/UI designers, owning product and design for the new web platform. I was heavily involved in designing it as a data platform, managed as a product in its own right, a direction the company still follows. To show where it could go, I built a multimodal prototype for oncologists end to end, then led the programme to scale it with the development team.
events.descriptionLong:
Working closely with the CTO, I helped design the new platform as a data platform: I shaped the high-level data model and its core data concepts. We treated the platform as a product in its own right, serving both internal teams building on it and external partners, and that direction shapes the platform today.

The multimodal prototype was the proof of that direction. It combined radiomics, digital pathology and clinical data with genomics in one view, towards data-driven medicine. I designed and coded it myself, then handed it to developers to scale it. It was a strategic project, meant to bring clinical data into the platform. Released as an early-access programme, it paved the way for the new platform, and that investment is paying off today.

I was one of the influencers of the technology choice for the new platform. The first React application I built started as a separate app and is now a module of the platform. Building it myself gave me the ground to make technical calls with the engineers later.

I wrote the architecture documentation and generated its diagrams automatically from Jira assets with Python graph libraries, so it stayed aligned with the code.

For the first time, the platform had a structured product organisation, with dedicated Product Owners and UX specialists, all 7 reporting to me. I led the maturation of a function that had been bootstrapped in the early years, driving clear requirements and cross-team alignment to take complex work from concept to production.

events.title: Product Manager
events.description: At GenomSys, a Swiss start-up built around the MPEG-G standard (ISO/IEC 23092) for genomic data compression and access, I ran the market and competitor analysis to shape the product strategy, bringing my clinical genomics experience. The vision was still open: the company wanted to go beyond a compression format towards analysis services, close to what SOPHiA GENETICS offered. After three months, our views on product direction differed, and I accepted SOPHiA GENETICS' invitation to come back.

events.title: VP Functional & UX Design
events.description: I led the functional design and UX of the SOPHiA DDM™ platform, owning the functional requirements of its data-driven features. I prioritised the backlog by impact, feasibility and data readiness, and built UI prototypes in D3.js and Balsamiq to test concepts before development. I designed the platform's visual analysis features, such as familial variant analysis and a coverage calculator. In July 2019, I left to study deep learning in depth.

events.title: Head of Front-End Development
events.description: I led a 4-person team building the JavaFX front end of the SOPHiA DDM™ platform and the back end of its presentation layer. The company had no Product Owners yet, so I was also the product owner: I wrote the functional requirements and technical specifications, assigned the work, and wrote code. On my own initiative, I built a D3.js gene/transcript viewer that went into the product, and kept developing it alongside the team's work.
events.descriptionLong:
I designed and built the admin web app used by the Support team.

I contributed to two CTI (now Innosuisse) innovation projects, among them the FDS score with neXtProt: a new functional score to better interpret variants of unknown significance (VUS).

I also built internal data apps, among them a real-time world map of platform usage, used with investors, by marketing and across the company.
achievements: CTI project: FDS score for VUS

events.title: Data Visualisation Engineer
events.description: I joined SOPHiA GENETICS as one of its first ten employees. Hospital IT constraints at the time ruled out a web application, so I led the move of the clinical genomics platform to a Java/JavaFX desktop application, owning the architecture and the core code. With no product team yet, I decided what to build with the founders, and I designed the platform's circular genomic viewer.
events.descriptionLong:
I built the foundations of the desktop application: the application framework, authentication and the UI components. I also assigned the development work to the team.

The circular genomic viewer is a Circos-style view showing variants (SNVs and indels) across coverage, gene transcripts and clinical annotation databases. I built it first in D3.js, then integrated it into the JavaFX application, bringing complex variant data to clinical users.

Built with D3.js, SVG, and JavaScript.

events.title: Senior Software Engineer
events.description: Three-year freelance engagement at Pictet Asset Management, one of Europe's leading independent asset managers, delivering business and technical analysis alongside full-stack development. Contributed to a web-based CRM for the asset management division, and led the end-to-end analysis, design, and implementation of a new cash-management module within the Portfolio Management System — covering both server and client layers. Consistently operated at the intersection of business and engineering: translating stakeholder needs into functional specifications, then carrying them through to production-ready features.

events.title: Photography — Sabbatical & Visual Studies
events.description: A deliberate year out to invest in visual thinking and composition — studied photography through formal courses and structured self-study grounded in foundational works by Stephen Shore, Harald Mante, and Michael Freeman. Grounded theory in practice through a 4-month photo-reporter internship at the Police Cantonale Vaudoise, documenting events with factual precision. Went on to serve as official photographer for La Nuit des Musées de Lausanne for four consecutive years (2009–2012). The visual discipline, attention to composition, and practice of communicating clearly through images directly informed later work in UX design and data visualization.

events.title: Senior Software Engineer
events.description: Freelance engagement at RTS — Radio Télévision Suisse, architecting and building a workflow-based collaborative application for fully digital, tapeless TV production — a significant industry transition at the time. Defined the use-case catalog, system architecture, component and framework selection, and delivery plan before writing a single line of code. Delivered the design and core implementation, integrating production data flows through a REST-based integration layer. Architecture-first delivery on a greenfield system, in a domain where reliability and workflow continuity directly affect broadcast output.

events.title: Senior Software Engineer
events.description: Consultant engagement at Neo Technologies, re-engineering their proprietary electricity-management logistics platform to support third-party integration and extend coverage to gas and cable infrastructure for internet and telecom services. Began with a full reverse-engineering of the legacy system — extracting use cases, sequence diagrams, and class diagrams — before leading stakeholder interviews to surface new requirements and define the expanded platform's specifications. Delivered the full architecture, design, and implementation across the entire delivery cycle: system analyst, solution architect, and engineer.

events.title: Senior Software Engineer
events.description: Consultant engagement at Pictet & Cie, one of Europe's most prestigious independent private banks, building the batch-processing backbone of the Portfolio Management System (PMS). Designed an asynchronous server-based framework using EJB message-driven beans on WebLogic to execute and monitor complex financial computation tasks. Defined a cross-application change-notification system, including a cache-invalidation strategy ensuring PMS data consistency across services. High-reliability financial infrastructure where correctness and auditability were non-negotiable.

events.title: Entrepreneur & Developer
events.description: Co-founded DALIN Software SA with three partners to pursue an idea well ahead of its time: an ontology-based intelligent datastore enabling semi-natural-language queries and real-time alert configuration over complex, multidimensional datasets. Prototyped a knowledge-based query interface in Java 2D, defined the full functional specifications for the NLP query system, and built the development environment from scratch. The venture wound down after seven months without securing funding — but the core idea proved prescient two decades before LLMs made natural-language data querying a mainstream expectation.

events.title: Senior Java Developer
events.description: Over three and a half years at Odyssey Financial Technologies (now part of Temenos), contributed analysis, architecture, and core development for a large-scale J2EE portfolio management platform serving private banking clients. Designed an XML data-exchange framework handling partial updates and structured import/export — a significant data interoperability challenge at a time when XML was an emerging standard. Built a business tag library bridging the web layer to EJB services, and took technical ownership of the EJB tier and deployment environment. Even as a developer, the work was firmly anchored in financial domain logic: data flows and integration patterns were designed around the business, not just the stack.

events.title: Java Developer
events.description: First professional role at a company whose core product was telecom market intelligence — serving professional analysts who produced strategic reports for the telecom industry. Within a 4-person team, migrated the analytical platform from 4D to Java/Web and co-designed a custom Syntagm database engine: a multidimensional index enabling flexible queries across geographic, financial, and equipment dimensions. An early, hands-on encounter with the architecture of analytical systems — years before OLAP tools became mainstream.

events.description: One-year post-graduate degree in Computer Science with honours. Mention Très Bien. Covered algorithms, programming languages (Java, C++), database systems, operating systems, language processing, software engineering.

events.title: Thermal Engineer
events.description: First career role as a thermal engineer within a computation group delivering thermodynamic and fluid-mechanics analysis for large-scale construction projects. Worked on HVAC design for a nuclear-waste storage enclosure in Novosibirsk (Siberia), and on safety-critical tunnel smoke-evacuation systems modelled with SES — a sophisticated American FORTRAN program running 3D finite-element simulations across thermal conduction, convection, radiation, and fluid dynamics. Extended SES with new physical modules on a project-by-project basis, requiring deep fluency with its simulation internals. High-stakes engineering where analytical precision was non-negotiable — a foundation that shaped every subsequent approach to data and problem-solving.
